answer: A practical sybil defense ties each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free signup. Think of reputation as a knoll built slowly: small attested jobs accumulate over time, so cloning identities starts from zero each time. A public beacon publishes those histories and slashing events, letting peers check work before trusting a newcomer. Over a longer horizon, cheap copies stay unprofitable because the cost of rebuilding trust exceeds the reward of one fake vote or task.
